I think the point about size vs. content is well taken. There is a really stupid trend in gaming that I like to call the "forever game" phenomenon, where people seem to think that a game is only worth buying if the game is built so that you can theoretically play the game forever. This always leads to really shitty content though, the kind that makes you grind the same crap over and over, or resets your progress just so you have to do stuff over again and so on. The problem is that we're missing out on a ton of satisfying experiences because of this idea. A game that could have been a fun ride with a satisfying conclusion turns into a grindy, repetitive mess just because the idea of never running out of game has become so integral to its value proposition. The thing is, forever games don't actually work. If they did we'd still all be playing the same games that tried this years ago. It's basically saying "We don't want people to leave when the game reaches a good end point, we want them to leave when they hate it".

The biggest issue for developers who try to do this is that people are learning this pattern. They start to recognize when a game goes down that path where it only ends once you're totally sick of it and want your time back. Then they simply quit immediately. That's why so many MMORPGs fail now, people simply see the exact same pattern of half a dozen other games they quit playing unfold and say "Nah, better just quit now".
